users.initial_password_hint: The user must change the initial password at first sign-in.

roles.name: Name
roles.builtin_hint: Built-in role – read only. Create a custom role for different permissions.

builtin_desc.system-admin: Full access to configuration, users and data (2FA required)
builtin_desc.security-analyst: Analyse alerts and events, maintain rules and assets
builtin_desc.auditor: Read only, including the audit log

wec.title: Windows integration (Event Forwarding)
wec.intro: Windows servers send their events agentlessly via Windows Event Forwarding (Kerberos, port 5985) to the appliance. Setup takes three steps.
wec.step1: 1. Define domain, appliance FQDN and target groups

roles_hint.dc: Security, Directory Service, DNS, System – one OU (distinguished name) per line.
roles_hint.member: Logons, processes, services, tasks, file access, PowerShell, Defender.
roles_hint.client: Lean selection: failed logons, local admins, Defender, services, USB.

wec.step2_text: Run the script as a domain administrator on a domain controller (with RSAT). It creates the service account, SPN, keytab and one GPO per role and links them to the OUs.
wec.step3_text: Upload the file siem-wec.keytab created by the script (principal {{principal}}), then delete it on the domain controller.
wec.check_text: Checks whether servers really apply the recommended audit policy (e.g. if the GPO is not applied yet). Run the script on a DC or via remoting for several servers – it changes nothing – and upload the generated JSON file here.
wec.audit_text: The GPO applies this advanced audit policy on all target systems.

devices.title: Devices (log sources)
devices.intro: Assign a device type to the sender IP. The pipeline picks the matching parser from it; for well-known formats it also detects the type itself.
devices.name: Name
devices.applied: Saved and active in the pipeline.
devices.not_applied: Saved. The pipeline could not be reloaded automatically – please restart Vector.

linux.title: Connect Linux servers
linux.intro: Agentless via rsyslog (syslog over TLS, port 6514) with optional auditd rules. Supports Debian/Ubuntu, RHEL family and SUSE.
linux.server: Appliance address (as seen from the servers)
linux.server_hint: Hostname or IP the Linux servers can reach; port 6514 must be allowed in the firewall for these servers.
linux.audit: Set up auditd rules (users, sudo, SSH, configuration files)
linux.step2_text: Run as root. The script installs rsyslog with the TLS module, stores the CA certificate, sets up forwarding and sends a test message. Then add the server under Devices with type “Linux server” or wait for auto-detection.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.intro: Disk guard every 5 minutes (warning at {{warn}} %, emergency cleanup at {{emergency}} %); backups and snapshots at night between {{start}}:00 and {{end}}:00.
maintenance.upd_howto: Apply: signed package with install.sh --upgrade (see manual).
maintenance.upd_uptodate: The appliance is up to date.
maintenance.diag_intro: Versions, status and error lines without secrets or event contents; names and addresses are pseudonymized. For the service provider.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.empty: No alerts in the selected period.
alerts.mitre_intro: Coverage of alert rules by MITRE ATT&CK (Enterprise): columns are tactics, boxes are techniques. A technique counts as covered if at least one enabled rule detects it. Reconnaissance and Resource Development cannot be seen in logs and are omitted.
alerts.mitre_summary: {{covered}} of {{techniques}} considered techniques covered, {{disabled}} only with a disabled rule, {{gaps}} gaps.

notify.title: Notifications
notify.intro: Alerts are sent by e-mail and/or Microsoft Teams (Workflows webhook).

ai.intro: Optional. Event data is pseudonymized before sending (names, addresses); the mapping stays local. Results are hints, not evidence.
ai.anonymize: Pseudonymization active for the custom endpoint
ai.forensics_intro: Analyzes related events of a user, host or address. Every statement must be backed by events; unsupported statements are discarded.

ar.title: Active response (FortiGate)
ar.intro: Blocks attacker addresses on the FortiGate. Off by default; private networks and the protection list can never be blocked. Blocks expire automatically.
ar.auto: Block automatically (selected high-severity rules only, at most 10 per hour)
ar.token: API token with write access (address objects)
ar.hint: Create the address group "{{group}}" on the FortiGate and reference it from a deny policy.

support.title: Support access (SSH)
support.intro: Time-limited access for the service provider: key only, from the given address only, read-only diagnostic commands (status, logs, containers). No access to event data, no shell. Expires automatically.

privacy.title: Privacy mode
privacy.intro: Optional. User names are shown as pseudonyms to analysts, auditors and management; administrators and privacy approvers see cleartext. Every change is logged.

retention.title: Retention per category
retention.intro: How long events are kept per category ({{min}}–{{max}} days). Older indices are deleted automatically.
retention.estimate: Estimated storage need: {{needed}} GB of {{total}} GB available.

sophos.title: Connect Sophos Central
sophos.intro: Events and alerts from Sophos Central. Primarily via the XDR Data Lake; without a license automatically via the SIEM integration API. Polled every 10 minutes. Create API credentials (client ID/secret) in Sophos Central under “Global Settings → API Credentials” with the role “Service Principal Read-Only”.
sophos.probe_datalake: Connection ok – XDR Data Lake available.
sophos.probe_siem: Connection ok – no Data Lake, SIEM API will be used.

changes.title: Change timeline
changes.intro: Who changed what and when: Active Directory, users and groups, GPOs, services, tasks and audit policy. Attribute changes show old → new.
changes.truncated: Result truncated – narrow the period or search.

snmp.title: Receive SNMP traps
snmp.intro: Traps from switches, NAS and servers (UDP 162). Supports v2c and v3. Source networks are controlled in the firewall (service “snmptrap”). Changes are applied automatically.
snmp.v2c_text: Stored: {{count}}. Entering a new list (one per line) replaces the existing ones; leave empty to keep.
snmp.v3_text: Preferred: authPriv with SHA-256 and AES-256. Devices should send informs; v3 traps require the sender engine ID.
snmp.engine_id: Device engine ID (optional, for v3 traps)
snmp.targets_text: Switches and devices polled every 60 seconds for interface status and reachability (UDP 161, IF-MIB).
snmp.name: Name
snmp.keys_hint: Empty key fields keep the stored key.
snmp.saved: Saved – the receiver picks up the change.

switches.title: Port matrix
switches.intro: Interface status of devices polled via SNMP (updated every minute).
switches.empty: No data yet. Add polling targets under Sources → SNMP traps → Polling targets.
switches.legend: Green: up · grey: down · dashed: administratively disabled.

assets.title: Asset center
assets.intro: End devices seen on the switches polled via SNMP (end-device ports only, uplinks excluded).
assets.empty: No devices yet. Requires SNMP polling targets with a readable MAC table.

fortigate.title: Connect FortiGate API
fortigate.intro: Reads the FortiGate ARP table and DHCP leases every 5 minutes and assigns IP and host name to each MAC address in the asset center. If an IP changes its MAC address, an “ip-mac-changed” event is recorded.
fortigate.token_hint: Create a REST API administrator in the FortiGate under System → Administrators; read-only profile (network/system), restrict access to the appliance address.
fortigate.pin_hint: For self-signed certificates: compare the fetched fingerprint with the device and accept it. Empty = verify against system certificates.
fortigate.test_ok: Connection ok – {{arp}} ARP entries, {{dhcp}} DHCP leases.

unparsed.title: Unrecognized sources
unparsed.intro: Events no parser was responsible for. Add the source under "Devices" with the right type, or report the format for a new parser.
unparsed.empty: No unrecognized events in the selected period.
unparsed.name: Name

archive.title: Tamper-evident archive
archive.intro: Every event is also written to hourly archive files. Completed hours are sealed (SHA-256, hash chain, signature); changes or deletions are detected by the verification.
archive.result_bad: {{n}} problems found – archive may have been tampered with.
archive.key_intro: Seals are signed with {{alg}}. A third party can verify the seals independently with this public key.
archive.ret_intro: Sealed files are deleted after expiry (nightly); every deletion is recorded in the seal chain. Allowed: {{min}}–{{max}} days.
archive.rest_intro: Loads a period into daily siem-restore-* indices after an integrity check (searchable like live data) and deletes them on expiry.
archive.tgt_intro: Optional: RFC 3161 timestamp per category (daily) and replication of sealed files to a directory (e.g. NFS/SMB mount) or S3 (with Object Lock). Local deletion only after confirmed replication.

cases.title: Cases
cases.intro: Bundle events, notes and evidence. Closing creates a signed, write-protected evidence package in the case archive.
cases.name: Title
cases.close_confirm: Close the case? It becomes immutable.

appr.title: Approvals (four-eyes principle)
appr.intro: When the four-eyes principle is on, archive restore, forensic export, closing critical alerts and revealing pseudonyms need approval by a second person.

disc.title: Discovery
disc.intro: Scans an internal network (max. 1024 addresses) for devices and suggests log sources. Only a few management ports are probed via TCP.
disc.mib_intro: Upload vendor MIBs (.mib, .my, .txt or ZIP) to resolve OID names. Files are never executed. Scalar OIDs need the suffix .0 in the polling target.

parsers.title: Parser editor
parsers.intro: Custom rules for events that would otherwise end up as “unparsed”: regular expression with named groups, mapped to ECS fields.
parsers.name: Name
parsers.regex_hint: Named groups: (?P<name>…). No lookarounds/backreferences, no single quote.
parsers.restart_note: Saving restarts Vector briefly; events stay in the buffer.
parsers.not_applied: Saved, but Vector could not be restarted.
parsers.import_error: Invalid file – expected a JSON export of the parser editor.
parsers.unsaved: Unsaved changes – choose “Save” to apply (imports and suggestions are validated and activated only then).

connect.title: Connect (TLS syslog)
connect.intro: CA certificate and ready-made configuration snippets for devices sending over TLS.
connect.snap_intro: Daily configuration backup; secrets are replaced by hash placeholders, changes stay visible.

dashboard.text: Overview of events, alarms and source health.
dashboard.example: Check each morning: any new alarms? Is every source still reporting?

reports.text: Creates and sends reports (e.g. weekly summary).
reports.example: Send a weekly report to management every Monday.

alerts.text: Shows triggered alarms; they can be acknowledged, commented and closed. The “MITRE ATT&CK” tab shows which attack techniques are covered by rules.
alerts.example: Multiple failed logins: open the alarm, check the user, then close it.

forensics.text: AI-assisted analysis: ask questions about log data in plain language.
forensics.example: "What did user mueller do last night?"

cases.text: Cases collect evidence for an incident and can be exported as a tamper-evident archive.
cases.example: Suspected data leak: create a case, attach events, close and export.

changes.text: Recorded changes on Windows systems and devices.
changes.example: Who changed the firewall rule yesterday?

unparsed.text: Sources whose messages are not understood yet.
unparsed.example: A new switch sends syslog: it shows up here, then assign a parser.

archive.text: Long-term archive of old data; archives can be restored temporarily.
archive.example: Restore last year's data for an audit.

devices.text: Directory of devices that send logs.
devices.example: Add a new firewall so its messages are attributed correctly.

assets.example: Check which hosts in the network are unknown.

switches.example: Find an unknown device on port 12.

windows.text: Connect Windows hosts via Windows Event Forwarding.
windows.example: Connect the domain controller to log sign-ins.

linux.example: Connect a new web server with the shown install command.

fortigate.example: Store the firewall's API token and test the connection.

snmp.example: The UPS reports a power failure: the trap appears as an event.

sophos.example: Enter API credentials; malware detections then appear as events.

discovery.example: Upload the vendor MIB so trap names are readable.

parsers.text: Editor for parsers that structure raw messages.
parsers.example: Parse messages of a special device with a custom parser.

connect.text: Connection snapshots: save and restore settings.
connect.example: Create a snapshot before changing settings.

ar.example: Block an attacker IP for one hour after brute force.

approvals.text: Four-eyes principle: sensitive actions need a second person's approval.
approvals.example: Request an archive restore; a colleague approves; repeat with the approval ID.

retention.text: Retention period and privacy mode (pseudonymised user names).
retention.example: Set retention to 180 days; enable privacy mode for the works council.

maintenance.example: Download the diagnostics package before contacting support.

notifications.text: E-mail delivery for alarms and reports (SMTP).
notifications.example: Enter the SMTP server and send a test mail.

syslog.example: Look for errors when no data arrives.

users.text: Create and lock user accounts and assign roles.

roles.text: Roles bundle permissions and data scope.

audit.example: Check who reset a password and when.

account.text: Manage your password, language and MFA.
account.example: Renew the MFA device after changing phones.
